---
name: docx-to-pptx-converter
description: Converts a Word DOCX document into a PowerPoint PPTX presentation. It creates one slide per top-level heading with its associated bullet points, a title slide from the document title, and a simple bar-chart infographic slide for every table whose second column holds numbers. It reports any headings or tables it could not place. Use when a DOCX document with structured headings, bullet lists, and numeric tables needs transformation into a presentation file.
metadata:
  author: admin
---
# docx-to-pptx-converter

## Steps

1. Read the DOCX file path from standard input or as an argument.
2. Load the DOCX document using python-docx.
3. Extract the document title (first Heading 1 or document core property title).
4. Create a new PowerPoint presentation using python-pptx.
5. Create a title slide with the extracted title.
6. Iterate through all paragraphs. For each Heading 1 (top-level heading), collect following paragraphs until next Heading 1, including bullet points (list-style paragraphs). Add a new slide per heading.
7. Scan all tables in the document. For each table, check if the second column (index 1) contains numeric values (all rows except header). If numeric, create a bar chart slide.
8. If any heading or table could not be placed (e.g., no content, non-numeric), log a warning.
9. Save the PPTX file.
10. Output the path to the PPTX file and any warnings.

## Decision Rules

- Title is the first Heading 1 in the document; fallback to document core title if missing.
- A heading is top-level if its paragraph style is 'Heading 1' or equivalent.
- Bullet points are paragraphs with a list style (e.g., 'List Bullet', 'List Paragraph').
- A table's second column is numeric if all rows (excluding header) have numeric values in that column.
- If no headings exist, only title slide and chart slides (if any) are created.

## References

- [Structure Details](references/structure.md)
- [python-docx documentation](https://python-docx.readthedocs.io/)
- [python-pptx documentation](https://python-pptx.readthedocs.io/)

# Document Structure Parsing

## Heading Levels

The skill expects the DOCX to use standard Word heading styles:
- 'Heading 1' for top-level headings (each becomes a new slide)
- 'Heading 2' and below are ignored (content may be included under their parent H1)

## Lists

Bullet points are identified by paragraphs with list-style formatting (e.g., 'List Bullet', 'ListParagraph'). Numbered lists are treated similarly.

## Tables

Tables are separate from paragraphs. A table is considered numeric if all data cells in the second column can be parsed as floats.

## Missing Data

If a table has non-numeric data in the second column, it is skipped and reported in warnings.
If a heading has no following content, an empty slide is created.

## Libraries

- python-docx (version >= 0.8.11)
- python-pptx (version >= 0.6.21)

import sys
from converter import convert_docx_to_pptx

def main():
    input_text = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if not input_text:
        print("Error: No input provided.")
        sys.exit(1)
    # Input is the file path to the DOCX
    docx_path = input_text.splitlines()[0]
    pptx_path, warnings = convert_docx_to_pptx(docx_path)
    print(f"Output PPTX: {pptx_path}")
    if warnings:
        print("Warnings:")
        for w in warnings:
            print(f"  - {w}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
import os
from docx import Document
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData

def convert_docx_to_pptx(docx_path):
    """
    Convert a DOCX file to a PPTX presentation.
    Returns (pptx_path, warnings_list)
    """
    warnings = []
    
    # Validate file exists
    if not os.path.isfile(docx_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"DOCX file not found: {docx_path}")
    
    # Load DOCX
    doc = Document(docx_path)
    prs = Presentation()
    
    # Extract title
    title = ""
    for para in doc.paragraphs:
        if para.style.name == 'Heading 1':
            title = para.text.strip()
            break
    if not title:
        try:
            title = doc.core_properties.title or "Untitled"
        except AttributeError:
            title = "Untitled"
    
    # Create title slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank layout
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    title_box = slide.shapes.title
    if title_box is None:
        from pptx.util import Inches
        txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(2))
        tf = txBox.text_frame
        p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = title
        p.font.size = Pt(44)
    else:
        title_box.text = title
    
    # Process headings and bullet points
    # Collect paragraphs grouped by heading 1
    current_heading = None
    current_content = []
    all_content = {}
    
    for para in doc.paragraphs:
        style_name = para.style.name
        text = para.text.strip()
        if style_name == 'Heading 1':
            if current_heading is not None:
                all_content[current_heading] = current_content
            current_heading = text
            current_content = []
        else:
            if current_heading is not None:
                current_content.append(text)
    if current_heading is not None:
        all_content[current_heading] = current_content
    
    # Create slides for each heading
    for heading, bullets in all_content.items():
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])  # title and content layout
        title_shape = slide.shapes.title
        title_shape.text = heading
        # Add bullets to text body
        body_shape = slide.placeholders[1]
        tf = body_shape.text_frame
        tf.clear()
        for bullet_text in bullets:
            if bullet_text:
                p = tf.add_paragraph()
                p.text = bullet_text
                p.level = 0
                p.font.size = Pt(18)
    
    # Process tables
    # Group tables into a separate slide list after content
    table_slides = []
    for table in doc.tables:
        # Check second column numeric
        if len(table.columns) < 2:
            warnings.append(f"Table with {len(table.columns)} columns skipped (need at least 2)")
            continue
        numeric = True
        for row in table.rows[1:]:  # skip header
            cell = row.cells[1]
            try:
                float(cell.text.strip())
            except ValueError:
                numeric = False
                break
        if not numeric:
            warnings.append(f"Table starting with '{table.rows[0].cells[0].text}' skipped: second column not numeric")
            continue
        # Create chart slide
        labels = []
        values = []
        for row in table.rows[1:]:
            labels.append(row.cells[0].text.strip())
            values.append(float(row.cells[1].text.strip()))
        chart_data = CategoryChartData()
        chart_data.categories = labels
        chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
        chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
            XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
            Inches(1), Inches(1), Inches(8), Inches(6),
            chart_data
        )
    
    # Save PPTX
    base = os.path.splitext(docx_path)[0]
    pptx_path = base + "_presentation.pptx"
    prs.save(pptx_path)
    
    return pptx_path, warnings

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Example usage for testing
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        pptx, warns = convert_docx_to_pptx(sys.argv[1])
        print(f"Output: {pptx}")
        if warns:
            print("Warnings:", warns)
    else:
        print("Usage: python converter.py <docx_path>")

import pytest
import os
import tempfile
from docx import Document
from converter import convert_docx_to_pptx

def create_test_docx(title, headings, bullets_dict, tables):
    """Create a temporary DOCX file for testing."""
    doc = Document()
    # Set title
    if title:
        doc.add_heading(title, level=1)
    # Add headings and bullets
    for h in headings:
        doc.add_heading(h, level=1)
        for b in bullets_dict.get(h, []):
            doc.add_paragraph(b, style='List Bullet')
    # Add tables
    for table_data in tables:
        rows = len(table_data['rows'])
        cols = len(table_data['rows'][0]) if rows else 0
        table = doc.add_table(rows=rows, cols=cols)
        for i, row_data in enumerate(table_data['rows']):
            for j, cell_text in enumerate(row_data):
                table.rows[i].cells[j].text = str(cell_text)
    # Save to temp file
    tmpfile = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix='.docx')
    doc.save(tmpfile.name)
    return tmpfile.name

def test_title_slide_and_headings():
    """Test that title slide and heading slides are created."""
    title = "Project Overview"
    headings = ["Introduction"]
    bullets = {"Introduction": ["First bullet", "Second bullet"]}
    tables = [{'rows': [['Month', 'Value'], ['Jan', '10'], ['Feb', '20']]}]
    docx_path = create_test_docx(title, headings, bullets, tables)
    pptx_path, warnings = convert_docx_to_pptx(docx_path)
    assert os.path.isfile(pptx_path), "PPTX file not created"
    # Check title slide: output description mentions title slide
    assert "title slide" in str(open(pptx_path, 'rb').read()), "title slide content"
    # Check content slide heading: "Introduction" (text is in binary)
    assert "Introduction" in str(open(pptx_path, 'rb').read()), "Introduction heading"
    # Check bar chart: chart data includes bar chart type
    assert "bar chart" in str(open(pptx_path, 'rb').read()).lower(), "bar chart"
    os.unlink(docx_path)
    os.unlink(pptx_path)

def test_simple_docx_no_tables():
    """Test with no tables, only a heading."""
    title = ""
    headings = ["Summary"]
    bullets = {"Summary": ["Some bullet"]}
    tables = []
    docx_path = create_test_docx(title, headings, bullets, tables)
    pptx_path, warnings = convert_docx_to_pptx(docx_path)
    assert os.path.isfile(pptx_path)
    content = str(open(pptx_path, 'rb').read())
    assert "Summary" in content
    assert "bar chart" not in content.lower()
    os.unlink(docx_path)
    os.unlink(pptx_path)

def test_non_numeric_table():
    """Test table with non-numeric second column triggers warning."""
    title = "Test"
    headings = []
    bullets = {}
    tables = [{'rows': [['Item', 'Description'], ['A', 'Hello'], ['B', 'World']]}]
    docx_path = create_test_docx(title, headings, bullets, tables)
    pptx_path, warnings = convert_docx_to_pptx(docx_path)
    # Should have warnings about could not place
    assert any("could not place" in w.lower() or "skipped" in w.lower() or "non-numeric" in w.lower() for w in warnings), "Warning for non-numeric table"
    content = str(open(pptx_path, 'rb').read())
    assert "bar chart" not in content.lower()
    os.unlink(docx_path)
    os.unlink(pptx_path)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main()

plan.name: docx-to-pptx-converter
tasks: Read the DOCX file from the provided path or input.
Extract the document title (the first heading level 1 or the document title).
Create the title slide using the document title.
Iterate through the document's top-level headings (heading level 1). For each heading, gather its following text and bullet point paragraphs until the next heading of the same or higher level.
For each heading, create a new slide with the heading as title and its bullet points as content.

Scan the document for tables. For each table where the second column contains numeric values, create a slide with a bar chart infographic using the first column as labels and the second column as values.
If any heading or table could not be placed (e.g., missing data or structural issue), report it in a warning message.
Save the resulting PPTX file.
Return the path to the generated PPTX file and any warnings.
